s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with discharge
salient_findings: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI
key_facts: 52-year-old Japanese woman
2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Pus discharge for 10 months
No trauma to the head
Otherwise healthy
No fever, headache, or nasal discharge
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Node size: 11 × 7 mm
High signal on T2-weighted MRI
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
Opacification of right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT
Expansion of right frontal and ethmoid sinuses
No bone destruction
Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis on histopathology

differentials: Erdheim-Chester disease variant with sinus involvement
per_call: Erdheim-Chester disease variant with sinus involvement

shortlist.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with discharge, consistent with blockage of the lacrimal duct

shortlist.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: Opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus on CT, with high signal on T2-weighted MRI and ring enhancement

shortlist.label: Pott's puffy tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid with pus discharge, suggestive of a subperiosteal abscess

shortlist.label: IgG4-related disease
shortlist.why_kept: Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate on histopathology, consistent with IgG4-related disease

shortlist.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with discharge, without evidence of infection or malignancy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a swelling on the right upper eyelid with pus discharge, combined with imaging findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal and ethmoid sinuses, and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus, is consistent with Pott's puffy tumor, a complication of frontal sinusitis.

rejected.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
rejected.why: Lack of symptoms related to the lacrimal gland or duct

rejected.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
rejected.why: Presence of pus discharge and inflammatory infiltrate suggests an infectious or inflammatory process rather than a mucocele

rejected.label: IgG4-related disease
rejected.why: Histopathology does not show characteristic IgG4-positive plasma cell infiltration

rejected.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
rejected.why: The presence of sinus opacification and expansion suggests a sinus-related process rather than an idiopathic orbital inflammation
